title: Joins & Set Operations
tagline: join algorithms, lateral, semi/anti joins, join order

placementQuiz.q: Nested Loop Join is best when:
options: One table is small, other has index on join key
placementQuiz.explain: NLJ: for each outer row, probe inner index. Best when outer is small and inner has index.

placementQuiz.q: Hash Join builds hash table on:
placementQuiz.explain: Hash Join: build hash on smaller (build) table, probe with larger. Memory-intensive.

options: Both tables sorted on join key
placementQuiz.explain: Merge Join: both inputs sorted on join key, then merged like merge sort. O(N+M).

options: Right side references left side columns
placementQuiz.explain: LATERAL: right subquery can reference columns from left. Like correlated subquery but in FROM.

options: Semi-join returns only left columns, stops at first match
placementQuiz.explain: Semi-join (EXISTS/IN): returns left rows only, stops at first match per left row. No duplication.

sections.title: Join Algorithms — How the Planner Executes

blocks.md: Planner picks algorithm: Nested Loop (small + index), Hash Join (large, no index), Merge Join (pre-sorted). EXPLAIN shows which. You can influence with indexes, stats, enable_* settings.

blocks.label: join algorithms in EXPLAIN
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL: primarily Nested Loop
-- Hash Join: 8.0.18+ (hash_join optimizer hint)
-- Merge Join: not directly controllable
blocks.py-pandas:
# No planner, but merge = merge sort join:
pd.merge(a, b, on='key', how='inner', sort=True)  # uses sort-merge

blocks.md: Hash Join: Build side (5000 rows) → hash table in memory. Probe side (10000 rows) → hash probe. If hash table > work_mem → spills to disk (slow). Increase work_mem for big joins.

items.q: Hash Join spills to disk when:
items.explain: work_mem controls hash table memory. Spill = massive slowdown. Increase work_mem or use indexes.

options: Tables already sorted on join key
Both tables have ORDER BY on join key
items.explain: Merge Join requires sorted input. Index scan or explicit sort provides ordering.

sections.title: LATERAL JOIN — Correlated Subquery in FROM

blocks.label: lateral basics
blocks.code:
-- For each employee, get their latest order
SELECT e.name, o.order_date, o.total
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT * FROM orders o
  WHERE o.emp_id = e.id
  ORDER BY o.order_date DESC
  LIMIT 1
) o ON true;

-- Equivalent correlated subquery (harder to read)
SELECT e.name,
  (SELECT order_date FROM orders o WHERE o.emp_id = e.id ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 1) AS latest_date,
  (SELECT total FROM orders o WHERE o.emp_id = e.id ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 1) AS latest_total
FROM employees e;
blocks.py-pandas:
# GroupBy + head(1)
latest = orders.sort_values('order_date').groupby('emp_id').head(1)
merged = employees.merge(latest, left_on='id', right_on='emp_id', how='left')
blocks.py-sqlalchemy:
# Lateral via subquery
from sqlalchemy import lateral
subq = session.query(Order).filter(Order.emp_id == Employee.id)
    .order_by(Order.order_date.desc()).limit(1).lateral()
session.query(Employee.name, subq.c.order_date, subq.c.total).outerjoin(subq).all()

before.use_case: Top-N per group, complex per-row logic

options: Columns from LEFT side of join
items.explain: LATERAL allows right side to see left side columns. Like correlated subquery in FROM.

items.q: CROSS JOIN LATERAL vs LEFT JOIN LATERAL:
options: CROSS = inner (drops left rows with no match), LEFT = preserves left
items.explain: CROSS JOIN LATERAL = INNER JOIN LATERAL. LEFT JOIN LATERAL preserves left rows (NULL if no match).

blocks.label: semi/anti join patterns
blocks.pg:
-- PostgreSQL: Semi-join optimization automatic
-- Hash Semi Join / Hash Anti Join in EXPLAIN
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL: Semi-join optimization (8.0+)
-- EXPLAIN shows 'Semi Join' or 'Anti Join'
blocks.py-pandas:
# Exists: merge + drop_duplicates on left key
merged = employees.merge(orders[['emp_id']].drop_duplicates(), 
                         left_on='id', right_on='emp_id', how='inner')

# Anti-join (left only)
merged = employees.merge(orders[['emp_id']].drop_duplicates(), 
                         left_on='id', right_on='emp_id', how='left', indicator=True)
result = merged[merged['_merge'] == 'left_only']

blocks.md: **"Not In" + subquery with NULL = zero rows.** Always use NOT EXISTS for anti-join. Or: `WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT emp_id FROM orders WHERE emp_id IS NOT NULL)`.

blocks.label: join order control
blocks.pg:
-- join_collapse_limit = 1 forces written order
-- pg_hint_plan for advanced control
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL: STRAIGHT_JOIN forces order
SELECT STRAIGHT_JOIN * FROM a JOIN b ON ...;
blocks.py-pandas:
# No planner; merge order = written order
df1.merge(df2).merge(df3)  # left-to-right

items.q: EXISTS vs IN semi-join: which stops at first match?
items.explain: Both are semi-joins — stop at first match per left row. EXISTS often clearer for complex conditions.
pg_hint_plan extension: /*+ Leading(a b c) */ forces join order.

blocks.sql: SELECT * FROM a FULL JOIN b ON a.id = b.id;
blocks.pg: SELECT * FROM a FULL JOIN b ON a.id = b.id;
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL: no FULL JOIN
SELECT * FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON ...
UNION
SELECT * FROM a RIGHT JOIN b ON ...;

items.title: FULL JOIN Workaround (MySQL)
items.statement: MySQL 5.7: write FULL JOIN using LEFT UNION RIGHT.

revisionCard: Nested Loop: small outer + indexed inner; Hash: large both, build hash on smaller; Merge: pre-sorted
LATERAL: right side sees left columns; CROSS JOIN LATERAL = inner, LEFT JOIN LATERAL = outer
Semi-join (EXISTS/IN): left columns only, stops at first match; Anti-join (NOT EXISTS): no match
NOT IN + subquery with NULL = disaster; always NOT EXISTS for anti-join
Join order: planner decides; join_collapse_limit=1 forces written order; pg_hint_plan for hints
FULL JOIN = LEFT UNION RIGHT; MySQL 5.7 workaround: LEFT UNION RIGHT

glossary.def: For each outer row, probe inner index. Best: small outer + indexed inner.
Build hash table on smaller input, probe with larger. Memory-heavy; spills to disk if > work_mem.
Both inputs sorted on join key; linear merge. O(N+M). Requires sorted input.
Right subquery references left columns. Like correlated subquery in FROM clause.
EXISTS/IN pattern — returns left rows only, stops at first match per left row.
NOT EXISTS pattern — returns left rows with NO match in right.
